scope: Reserve a bounded listener slot before TCP Accept, preventing ordinary HTTP/TLS connection goroutines from growing without an application connection-count limit.
The shared pool includes raw HTTP, TLS handshakes/connections and hijacked WebSockets until their actual transport closes. It is separate from existing WebSocket upgrade/read-pump admission.
Saturation waits in the kernel connection backlog; it creates no per-waiter application goroutine and does not evict an existing player or add account/IP bans.
One-time connection/listener closure frees capacity and wakes blocked accepts safely; main retains HTTP/TLS serving and graceful shutdown paths.

operatorConfiguration.relationship: Combined pool overlaps the separate -ws-max-connections pool (default512); use HTTP capacity above the chosen WS cap to leave ordinary HTTP headroom. Neither number demonstrates active-player capacity.
operatorConfiguration.saturation: Listener-level waiting, not HTTP503. Existing WS-specific overload can still return HTTP503 after HTTP admission.

checks.configuration: Invalid limits rejected; minimum, default and maximum pool sizes retained.
checks.actualHTTPPool: Two occupied keepalive connections keep a third request pending; closing one allows the exact waiting request to succeed without increasing pool size.
checks.actualCloseAndShutdown: Closing a saturated listener wakes blocked Accept; duplicate closes release the admitted transport reservation exactly once.
checks.actualHijackedSocket: Production upgrader supports message echo; handler return does not release the active WebSocket's slot. Closing its transport admits a waiting HTTP request.
checks.actualTLSPool: Trusted disposable TLS fixture holds the shared single slot across a successful request; a second TLS handshake waits until transport closure, then completes its exact HTTP request.

combinedProtocolRace.scope: Current production changes and first four new connection groups, before adding the TLS-only test.

finalHTTPRace.scope: Final source including all five new connection groups, HTTP deadlines, health and retained WS admission checks.

limits: Actual in-process loopback HTTP/TLS/hijack checks with small pools, not latest-binary authenticated database/restart, public proxy/TLS or measured player-capacity acceptance.
A waiting TCP connection can still exist in the kernel backlog. This is an accepted application-transport bound, not total raw network, kernel, proxy or upstream denial-of-service protection.
TLS uses a trusted test certificate, not public certificate/renewal or owner-deferred IPv6 proof.
Other background worker bounds, jump policy and latest-source connected/load evidence remain open; milestone1.72 is not complete.
